medium_value.description: Define separate immutable pins for the Sprint 2 harness baseline and the Sprint 3 smoke implementation. Record both commits and the actual container digest in smoke metadata, and require the smoke to execute the Sprint 3 mount changes.

Make refusal reruns retain immutable attempt records, consume the same spend cap, and apply a specified final-row selection rule. Test a second refusal, an infrastructure failure on retry, and resume after the first attempt.

Treat observed project-scope execution during the spike as a containment failure: run the spike with blocked egress, a bounded spend limit, and an explicit credential exposure boundary before using its transcript as evidence.

Name the immutable model artifact used for the scope spike and record the exact scope flags, effective settings, and framework content hashes. Repeat the scope assertions if any of those inputs change before the smoke.

Require the final Sprint 3 combination of grader 1.5, registration v2, finding validators, mount changes, and seeding library to pass an integrated self-check, and record that final pipeline version before release.

Define how all four finding validators consume or derive from the canonical contract, and run the same valid and invalid corpus through every validator, including alias normalization and path-boundary cases.
Specify that an invalid finding produces an explicit gate error or blocking violation, with tests for reports containing only invalid findings and reports mixing valid and invalid findings.

Make sweep manifests a complete partition of the frozen inventory: reject duplicate IDs, missing IDs, unknown IDs, and conflicting categories before mutations. Define overflow handling when the inventory exceeds seven batches of 40.
Move independent sample verification before closure application, or specify a reversible apply log and automatic reopening of affected closures before a disputed batch is re-swept.

Replace relative quarantine expiry such as next cycle close with a machine-checkable deadline and define how cycle closure triggers expiration. Report full-suite executed, skipped, and quarantined totals separately.

Add an explicit dependency from consensus-integrity work to the paged-fetch changes and assign integration ownership for shared Bridgebuilder files. Update sprint close instructions to enumerate the actual patch producers.

Specify the outcome when the single permitted smoke fails: keep G-4 incomplete and block dependent drift-test removal and release acceptance, or explicitly amend the acceptance requirement through a DEC decision.
Verify release reachability against freshly fetched remote main using an ancestry check, and verify the remote tag target and GitHub prerelease metadata after publication.
Define the spike and smoke budget relationship, including whether the USD 2 spike comes from the USD 30 smoke allocation, and enforce the shared allocation before launching either run.
Add a cycle-wide spend reservation and stop rule for Bridgebuilder and dissent runs, including failed attempts and retries. Define the action when funds run out before an approval gate succeeds.

Reconcile existing-tag refusal with crash recovery: accept an existing tag only when its target and release identity match the verified candidate, and reject conflicting tags. Test crashes after tag creation, release creation, and ledger push.

Make publication preconditions state-aware on rerun. Recognize the verified ledger commit already pushed by this candidate, and preserve a durable deferred ledger artifact when another commit advances main.

Specify how v1 candidates satisfy the new reachability and integrity guarantees: validate or upgrade their targets and inputs before publication, and refuse candidates that cannot meet those guarantees.
Add release tests that advance main between the initial remote check and tag creation, and explicitly define whether publication accepts a verified descendant of merge_sha or aborts.

Require a successful egress self-check on the actual image, network configuration, and model endpoint used by the spike and smoke. Treat a quarantined egress test as insufficient authorization to launch those runs.
Define and test a reboot-persistent supervisor lifecycle, including startup restoration, persisted run arguments, and reconciliation after host restart for both systemd and fallback modes.

Resolve the contradiction about which pipeline version the Sprint 3 smoke runs at. Task 3.1 and Task 3.4 say 'the Sprint 2 pin'; the Sprint 3 Dependencies say 'the Sprint 3 head is the recorded pin for the smoke'. Since the smoke exercises the home-scope mount (built in Task 3.1), it cannot run on the Sprint 2 harness tree. State explicitly: image digest = loa-ablation:259 (Sprint 2), harness tree = the Task 3.1 commit, and define which value is written into meta and into the README pipeline-version table.

Add to Task 3.2: npm run build, dist/ committed and check-bb-dist-fresh green (the task changes FindingsBlockSchema and the Bridgebuilder persona), and a grader 1.5 regression run asserting every 1.4 fixture grades identically except the new judge-verdict cases, mirroring the 1.4 rule in Task 2.3.

Run the Task 3.0 spike inside the egress block (loa-egress network, allowlist from the registry) and record every denied connect, so the allowlist gaps for Claude Code's non-model endpoints (version check, telemetry, OAuth) are found at ≤ USD 2 rather than during the USD 30 smoke.

When the Task 2.4 container bats are quarantined in CI, require the lead to run them locally (Docker 26.1.5 is a listed dependency) and attach the output path as Sprint 2 E2E evidence; a quarantine row alone should not satisfy the egress part of G-8.

Estimate the cycle PR's changed-file count (four sprints, committed dist/, fixtures, removed 4.5 K fixture lines) against the 3,001-file cap and the default excludes, and define the G-2 verdict if the cycle-branch Bridgebuilder run reports degraded_reason or falls back to exit 3: whether G-2 is unmet, whether a reduced-scope re-run counts, and what it costs against the USD 20 share.

Define the fallback if the C-3 v2 publish path fails irrecoverably at the real rc.8 publish (first real exercise of new code): e.g., generate a v1 candidate and publish through the old path (Task 1.3 keeps v1 publishable), file a bead, and record a DEC row; state that the tag-on-merge requirement still holds under the fallback.

Specify how PRD FR-10 AC 3's 'planted-PR-hook never loaded' assertion is satisfied if Task 3.0 selects design (c) (contract text plus clause (f)): name the test that proves it under (c), or amend the acceptance to the (c)-form so Sprint 3 cannot be unapprovable by construction.

Split Task 3.4 so harness README completion, evals/README.md index and CHANGELOG entries are not gated on the smoke being green; keep only the drift-test deletion behind the smoke gate and name its fallback (test stays, bead filed) if the smoke does not pass.

Add a branch-protection preflight to Task 4.4 before publish (read the main branch protection rules via gh api and predict whether the --force-with-lease ledger push can succeed), and name the owner and bead for a deferred ledger commit so 'ledger_commit: deferred' has a follow-up.

Add a schedule-slip rule for the unattended run: whether sprint dates are targets that shift (and the cycle simply takes longer) or hard, and what the lead does if Sprint 4's one day ends before publish. Note Sprint 4 contains seven Explore batches, lead triage of every closure row, a 10 % re-verification, possibly multiple Bridgebuilder rounds with fix cycles, review, audit, merge, record, publish and archive.

State that implementer A begins the Task 3.0-invariant parts of Task 3.1 (check_mount_closed clause (e), took-effect.sh clause (f) pr_bytes_read, the grader negative-control fixture, bats scaffolding) while the spike runs, and that only the mount-mode and contract-text branch waits on the spike outcome.

Add an explicit sprint-close task to Sprint 4 (mirroring Tasks 1.7, 2.6, 3.5) that runs /review-sprint and /audit-sprint, and place it in Task 4.4's sequence BEFORE the admin merge and publish. State what is reviewed (sweep report, release metadata, any Bridgebuilder-triggered fixes) and that no commit lands on the cycle branch after the audit without re-audit.

Mark the repair-vs-quarantine decision for each of the ten failing tests in Task 1.6 as a lead judgment (or give the implementer a mechanical rule: a fix is 'local' only if it touches test files or the function under test and changes no shipped behaviour), and require the implementer to list each decision in the patch return for a DEC row.

Define the channel through which implementers report judgment calls made inside mechanical tasks (e.g., a mandatory 'Judgment calls' section in the patch return naming the alternatives rejected), so Task 1.7/2.6/3.5's 'DEC rows for every implementer judgment call' has a source.

State in Task 4.3/4.4 that any fix landed after the CHANGELOG is stamped to [2.0.0-rc.8] (Bridgebuilder-triggered fixes in Task 4.4) is appended to the rc.8 section and to the release notes before the merge, and that Task 4.3's version stamps and checksums are re-verified afterwards.

Clarify the egress self-check: Task 2.5 says 'tools only, no model spend' while the Sprint 2 risk mitigation says self-check 'requests each planned model'. Specify that the probe is a connectivity or auth-only call (no completion tokens) and name the endpoint shape, or budget the small spend.

Before deleting the 4.5 K committed power-mini fixture lines in Task 2.2, assert that synth.py --seed 20261023 reproduces them byte-identically in the CI Python version, and record the assertion as a test that stays.

Place evals/fixtures/review-prs/external-candidates.md (Task 3.3) outside the path that Task 1.6 marks linguist-generated -diff, or exempt *.md at that fixture root, so the file remains reviewable in implementer patches and in the Bridgebuilder's PR diff.
Define the Bridgebuilder 'plateau rule' referenced in Task 4.4 within this plan (e.g., stop after a round that adds no new HIGH or MEDIUM finding, maximum N rounds within the USD 20 share).

State the rule for choosing pr-20 versus pr-16 for the smoke (e.g., pr-20 unless its changed_files exceed the overlay's tested range), and the rule for the sweep if the frozen inventory exceeds 7 × 40 beads.

Define the outcome when the three dissent runs are exhausted and review or audit is still not APPROVED: e.g., the lead writes a DEC row listing the unresolved findings, marks the sprint BLOCKED, sets run state to a halt-awaiting-operator value, and does not start the next sprint. Apply the same rule to a review that returns a HIGH the lead disagrees with.

Define smoke failure handling precisely: (a) what counts as a 'launch' for the 'launched once' rule (a session that reaches the model vs. one that aborts on infrastructure_error with near-zero spend); (b) whether an infrastructure-aborted launch may be re-launched within the remaining USD 30; (c) the Sprint 3 acceptance verdict if the smoke completes with oracle_exposed_defects > 0 and is not re-launched — is G-4 recorded as unmet, and can the sprint still be APPROVED on the clause (e)/(f) bats alone as the Risks section implies?

Sequence or split tasks that have two parallel implementers editing the same files: Sprint 2 Task 2.1 (A) and Task 2.4 (D) both modify pipeline-run.sh and blind-session.sh; Task 2.3 (C) and Task 2.4 (D) both modify run-ablation.sh; Sprint 3 Task 3.2 (B) and Task 3.3 (C) both modify registration.py for schema v2; Tasks 2.3, 3.1, 3.3 and 3.4 all edit evals/harness/README.md. Either assign the shared file to one task, state the landing order and require the later implementer to rebase onto the applied patch, or give one owner the registration.py v2 change with both features.

Assign the Task 3.0 spike's ≤ USD 2 to a named spend share (it is not in the 30/20/50 split) and add a running spend line per share to every sprint report and the sprint-close tasks, so the USD 100 cap is enforced mechanically. Also estimate the Bridgebuilder cost per round from the PR #1289 rounds and state how many Sprint 4 rounds the USD 20 share permits.

Reconcile the bead counts and add an appendix listing every Tier 1 bead with its task: Sprint 1 Success Metrics say '13 beads closed' but the tasks name 12 (bd-ra4im, bd-cpvc6, bd-kwloh, bd-mgun5, five in 1.5, three in 1.6); Sprint 2 says '11 beads' but the tasks name 13 (two in 2.1, seven in 2.2, two in 2.3, two in 2.4). Tasks 3.1 and 3.2 name no beads at all.

Clarify how G-6 CI evidence is obtained in Sprint 1 when the cycle PR does not exist until Task 4.4: either name the push-triggered workflow runs on the cycle branch as the Sprint 1 evidence, or move the G-6 part of Task 1.E2E to Sprint 4 and make Sprint 2's dependency 'Sprint 1 CI' refer to a local or branch-run result.

Replace the quarantine expiry 'next cycle close' with a concrete ISO date (or a rule the expiry gate can evaluate, e.g., 30 days from the quarantine commit) so check-quarantine-expiry.sh has a comparable value, and state the expiry used in the QUARANTINE.tsv column definition.

Define the pinned pipeline version as a tree hash (or the commit after Task 2.5 including its own README change) rather than 'the Sprint 2 head', since Task 2.6 adds commits (CHANGELOG, DEC rows, checksums) after the pin is recorded. State that docs-only commits do not invalidate the pin and that reproduce.sh compares the named trees.

blockers.concern: Admin merge is planned with CI green, but the required checks and their binding to the final reviewed commit are not enumerated.
blockers.why_matters: An admin merge can bypass protections, and checks or approvals from an earlier head can be mistaken for evidence covering the final changes.
blockers.location: Task 4.4: Bridgebuilder rounds, CI green and admin merge
blockers.recommendation: Define the required check and approval set, verify every result against the exact final head SHA, and invalidate affected evidence after any subsequent patch before performing the merge.

blockers.concern: Candidate digests are described without an independent trust binding, and the ledger patch has no explicit path or content restrictions.
blockers.why_matters: Changing an input together with its digest can evade a consistency check, and a validly hashed patch could modify files beyond the release ledger.
blockers.location: Task 1.3: candidate v2, digest checks and post-merge-ledger.patch
blockers.recommendation: Bind the candidate to a trusted immutable commit or protected artifact, validate every ref update, and restrict the ledger patch to expected paths and schema transitions. Test mutation of both an input and its recorded digest.

blockers.concern: Egress enforcement tests may be quarantined while G-8 and the harness release still pass.
blockers.why_matters: A claimed security boundary could ship without having been exercised in a container environment.
blockers.recommendation: Require the complete container egress suite on the release image before enabling blocked mode for credential-bearing runs. Quarantine may explain missing evidence but must not satisfy that gate.

blockers.concern: Existing-tag refusal conflicts with crash-safe idempotent reruns, and v1 candidates remain publishable without a stated compatibility safety rule.
blockers.why_matters: A crash after tag creation can block recovery, while a legacy candidate may bypass the new target and integrity requirements.
blockers.location: Task 1.3: existing-tag refusal, verified-or-performed steps and v1 compatibility
blockers.recommendation: Specify a state machine that accepts an existing tag only when its target and release identity exactly match the candidate. Upgrade or reject v1 candidates unless all v2 safety invariants can be established.

blockers.concern: Invalid Failure clauses are excluded from verdict tallies, but the plan does not state that any such violation makes the gate fail.
blockers.why_matters: A malformed blocking finding could disappear from the tally and produce an approval.
blockers.recommendation: Make validation violations produce an explicit non-approving outcome and nonzero exit status. Add cases containing only invalid blockers and mixtures of valid low-severity findings with invalid blockers.

blockers.concern: Publication checks remote main before creating the tag and release, leaving a race in which main changes after the check.
blockers.why_matters: The ledger push lease protects that push only; it does not make the earlier tag and release operations conditional on the checked main state.
blockers.recommendation: Define the required invariant at each publication step, re-fetch and verify remote ancestry immediately before publication, and test main advancing or being rewritten between every externally visible operation.

blockers.concern: Supervisor recovery is based on locks, PIDs and unit-name patterns without a specified durable ownership identity or provider-request reconciliation.
blockers.why_matters: After reboot or PID reuse, recovery could terminate unrelated work or launch a duplicate paid session while the original provider request continues.
blockers.location: Task 2.4: batch supervisor, orphan reconciliation and resume
blockers.recommendation: Persist boot ID, process start identity, attempt ID and provider request/session ID. Reconcile uncertain requests before retrying, terminate the complete owned process group, and test reboot, PID reuse and cancellation during an active request.

blockers.concern: The 3,001-file cap, omitted patches and default exclusions are tested, but their required effect on an approving verdict is unspecified.
blockers.why_matters: A partial review can report approval despite missing the files containing the decisive defect.
blockers.recommendation: Define verdict eligibility for each degraded_reason and coverage deficit. Require a non-approving outcome when required coverage is incomplete, and test cap, missing-patch, oversize and excluded-security-file cases.

blockers.concern: The USD 100 cap excludes subagents, and the plan does not state how the spike, retries, fallback providers and concurrent sessions consume a shared budget.
blockers.why_matters: Per-session limits and a dissent-run count do not enforce an aggregate spending limit, especially when unattended workers retry.
blockers.recommendation: Define the complete billable scope, charge the spike to a named allocation, and use atomic shared reservations covering workers and retries. Stop launches when usage is unknown or remaining funds cannot cover the reservation.

blockers.concern: The egress denial container bats (github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, direct IP, IPv6, redirect, CONNECT, external DNS) may be satisfied "in the Docker-enabled CI job or with a dated quarantine row". A quarantine row lets FR-9 AC 2 and the Task 2.5 pin pass with the egress block never demonstrated, and the Sprint 3 smoke then "runs under the egress block" on that assumption.
blockers.why_matters: The egress block is the control that keeps a sandboxed model from reaching the upstream repository (bd-ijxuk: nine bare sessions already did). Shipping it with its only end-to-end evidence quarantined means the pipeline version is pinned on an unverified security property, and the USD 30 smoke runs without it.
blockers.location: Sprint 2 Task 2.4 (container bats clause), Task 2.5 pin, Sprint 3 Security Considerations
blockers.recommendation: Make the egress denial suite a hard precondition for Task 2.5 and for launching the Task 3.1 smoke: if the Docker CI job is unavailable, run the suite on the operator host and attach `egress-proxy.bats` output plus `meta/egress-denied.jsonl` as evidence; exclude the denial cases from the quarantine mechanism entirely.

blockers.concern: The enrichment guard compares selected finding fields but does not explicitly preserve the failure scenario, explanation, evidence or recommendation.
blockers.why_matters: A writer could preserve IDs and severity while changing the substance of a finding, including the Failure clause later used for judging.
blockers.location: Task 1.2: semantic equality; Task 3.2: canonical finding contract
blockers.recommendation: Identify every authoritative finding field and require exact canonical equality for those fields. Reject duplicate IDs and test altered scenarios, evidence and recommendations with unchanged comparison keys.

blockers.concern: The home-scope overlay removes an enumerated executable surface (`skills/ commands/ agents/ hooks/ settings*.json`) but omits other PR-controlled paths Claude Code loads at project scope: `.mcp.json` (launches MCP server processes), root `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/CLAUDE.md` (prompt injection), `.claude/output-styles/`, `.claude/plugins/`. The Task 3.0 spike plants only a hook, a skill and a CLAUDE.md line, so an `.mcp.json`-based execution path would pass the spike and the clause (e) check unobserved.
blockers.why_matters: G-4 claims PR-supplied `.claude/` content is data only. A PR under review that ships an `.mcp.json` server definition could execute arbitrary code in the reviewing session, exposing the oracle and the operator credentials inside the sandbox, while every acceptance criterion in FR-10 still passes.
blockers.location: Sprint 3 Task 3.0 (spike planted set), Task 3.1 (`lib/sandbox-mount.sh` home-scope executable surface, `check_mount_closed` clause (e))
blockers.recommendation: Derive the executable surface from the pinned Claude Code version's documented load paths rather than a hand list; add `.mcp.json`, root `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `output-styles/`, `plugins/` to the removed set; plant one of each in the spike (the MCP server writing a canary file); make clause (e) assert the overlay contains none of these paths by denylist, with a bats case per path.

blockers.concern: The plan permits fixing an oracle exposure after the only smoke and substituting clause (e)/(f) bats for another smoke, despite acceptance requiring a successful smoke.
blockers.why_matters: The shipped configuration could have no successful end-to-end evidence that the exposure was removed.
blockers.location: Sprint 3 Acceptance Criteria; Risks & Mitigation; Task 3.4
blockers.recommendation: Make a failed smoke leave G-4 incomplete. Reserve budget for verification after a fix, or explicitly defer shipping the feature when a successful smoke cannot be obtained.

blockers.concern: The proxy plan specifies hostname allowlisting but does not define DNS resolution enforcement, redirects to private addresses, proxy-port restrictions or access to host services.
blockers.why_matters: An allowed hostname or an unintended proxy capability could provide access outside the intended model endpoints.
blockers.recommendation: Restrict methods and destination ports, reject private/link-local/loopback destinations after resolution, define DNS behavior, and test host-gateway access, address rebinding and proxy configuration failure.

blockers.concern: The record commit uses prev and head as parents, but the secret scan covers only the exported staged tree.
blockers.why_matters: Pushing the record ref also makes its parent history reachable. A clean staged tree does not establish that newly published ancestor objects contain no secrets or excluded material.
blockers.location: Task 1.4: staged-tree scan and commit-tree -p prev -p head
blockers.recommendation: Define whether parent history is already trusted and public. Scan newly reachable objects before pushing, or use a history structure that does not introduce unscanned ancestry.

blockers.concern: The scope spike treats absence from a transcript and process list as proof that planted project instructions, skills and hooks never loaded.
blockers.why_matters: Instructions may load silently, and short-lived hooks may exit before process inspection. PR-controlled instructions could influence a session that holds model credentials.
blockers.recommendation: Use planted canaries with deterministic filesystem or invocation-log effects, capture process execution events throughout the session, and assert the effective configuration and CLI version.

blockers.concern: The smoke's execution pin is contradictory: Task 3.1 requires the Sprint 2 pin, while Sprint 3 dependencies require the Sprint 3 head. The Sprint 2 pin predates the HOME-scope implementation being validated.
blockers.why_matters: The smoke could validate an older harness while being cited as evidence for the new mount implementation.
blockers.recommendation: Define separate immutable framework, harness, fixture and image identifiers. Require the smoke to execute the candidate containing Task 3.1 and record every identifier in its metadata.

blockers.concern: The tool-grammar denylist and writer-role allowlist do not establish a fail-closed capability contract for every API and headless adapter.
blockers.why_matters: Output validation happens after generation and cannot prevent a tool invocation that an adapter accidentally enabled.
blockers.location: Task 1.2: writer_role_allowlist and per-adapter no-tools tests
blockers.recommendation: Require each allowed adapter to prove tools, shell access and external integrations are disabled at invocation time. Reject unknown adapter versions or unsupported capability configurations and test attempted tool calls.
